song.title: Statesboro Blues (Live at the Filmore East)

guitar.evidence: Duane Allman's Gibson Les Paul (and slide work) and Dickey Betts' Gibson Les Paul/SG use are well documented in Southern rock history.

tone.target: raw Duane-style slide crunch with bright mid bite
tone.profile: raw Duane-style slide crunch with bright mid bite
tone.summary: A crunchy, bite-focused signal chain using a Tube Screamer boost into a UK 45/UK 50 style amp, paired with a vintage cabinet and subtle room ambience for that live, raw feel.

rig.name: The Allman Brothers Band - Statesboro Blues (Live at the Filmore East) - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up ambient noise and hum from the live recording source.
Simulate the Tube Screamer emphasis and provide mid-range bite without excessive warmth.
blocks.gap: The dedicated TS model is absent, so 'Boost' is used to emulate its tightening effect.

blocks.purpose: Add raw crunch and bite characteristic of classic blues/slide guitar tones.
blocks.gap: The 'Red Haze' or 'Distortion' models might be too modern; RAT-style provides the necessary aggressive, biting edge.

alternatives.model: Red Haze (if more sustain is desired)

blocks.purpose: Emulate the Marshall/Plexi edge and provide classic British breakup tone.
Provide the required classic British 4x12 cabinet sound.

alternatives.model: UK Basket 4x12 (if a more open, less defined tone is needed)

blocks.purpose: Enhance the upper-mid bite and cut low end to focus on slide phrasing clarity.

alternatives.model: Guitar EQ 1 (if less aggressive shaping is desired)

blocks.purpose: Create the required dry live room feel without adding excessive wash or delay.

alternatives.model: Plate (if a more defined reverb is preferred)

improvements.summary: Enhance the cabinet realism with a more vintage, raw IR to better capture the 'raw Duane-style' slide crunch and upper-mid bite.

proposals.reason: Enhance raw, biting mid-range for slide phrasing clarity.
